submission.bindingBasis: The owner has changed (workspace no longer present in current open inventory), and the exact replay probe already returned already_closed/removed=false, but that probe result is planning-time evidence whose current applicability is unproven. The transport observation indicates the close commit may have already succeeded without a trustworthy response, so the outcome is genuinely unknown rather than simply uncommitted.
submission.rationale: The consequence boundary evidence states outcomeUnknown=true and ownerChanged=true. The workspace is absent from the open inventory, but the generic signal does not prove WHICH close request caused that removal — it could have been this exact close (in which case replay would be safe/exact, if the tombstone still exists) or a later close of a different world state (in which case replaying this close could create a duplicate or misattribute the effect). The planning-time probe (already_closed/removed=false) was correct at planning time but current applicability is unproven, and the owner action contract requires that an exact close tombstone retains sourceStateDigest after physical removal — which I cannot confirm without reobserving. Acting unbound or with stale planning binding risks either inventing a second effect or misapplying a stale tombstone. HOLD would preserve nothing useful since the owner may have changed identity. REPLAY_EXACT is only justified if the current close tombstone state is verified. Reobservation is the required step to determine whether the tombstone with the exact sourceStateDigest still exists.
